# How do I appeal a parking citation in San Francisco online?
1. Open your web browser and go to the SFMTA parking tickets page: https://www.sfmta.org/pay-or-contest-parking-ticket

claims.objective: Open https://www.sfmta.org/pay-or-contest-parking-ticket and check for the button labeled "Pay or Contest Parking Tickets".

span.text: 2. On that page click the button labeled "Pay or Contest Parking Tickets".

claims.objective: Click the button labeled "Pay or Contest Parking Tickets" and check that the next page shows a link or button labeled "Contest a Citation".

span.text: 3. On the next page, click the link or button labeled "Contest a Citation".

claims.objective: Click the link or button labeled "Contest a Citation" and check for a button labeled "Continue" on the resulting form page.

span.text: 4. Enter the citation number and license plate (or other requested identifying info) in the fields shown, then click "Continue".

claims.objective: Enter the citation number and license plate (or other requested identifying info) in the fields shown, click "Continue", and check for options such as "Request Administrative Review" or "Request a Hearing".

span.text: 5. When prompted, choose the type of contest you want (for example "Request Administrative Review" or "Request a Hearing") by clicking the corresponding option, then click "Continue" or "Next".

claims.objective: Choose the contest type by clicking the option labeled "Request Administrative Review" or "Request a Hearing", then click "Continue" or "Next" and check for the online contest form fields.

span.text: 6. Fill out the online contest form:

claims.objective: Fill out the online contest form and check that the form includes fields to select a reason and enter an explanation.

span.text: - Select the reason for your appeal from the provided options.

claims.objective: Select the reason for your appeal from the provided options and check that an option you can choose is visible.

span.text: - Type a clear statement explaining why the ticket should be cancelled.

claims.objective: Type a clear statement explaining why the ticket should be cancelled and check that the text you entered appears in the explanation field.

span.text: - Attach supporting evidence (photos, meter receipts, permits) using the "Attach file", "Upload", or "Choose File" button.

claims.objective: Attach supporting evidence using the "Attach file", "Upload", or "Choose File" button and check for the presence of one of those buttons.

span.text: 7. Review your information and then click the button labeled "Submit" or "Submit Request" to send your contest.

claims.objective: Review your information and click the button labeled "Submit" or "Submit Request" and check for a confirmation or confirmation number on the screen.

span.text: 8. Note the confirmation number shown on the screen and/or any confirmation email. If you’re required to pay a deposit to request a hearing, follow the instructions on-screen (buttons may be labeled "Pay" or "Pay Deposit").

claims.objective: Note the confirmation number shown on the screen and follow any on-screen instructions, checking for a button labeled "Pay" or "Pay Deposit" if a deposit is required.

span.text: 9. Monitor your email for the SFMTA’s decision or further hearing instructions. If you requested a hearing, follow the instructions in the notice to appear by mail, phone, in-person, or virtual hearing as specified.

claims.objective: Monitor your email for the SFMTA’s decision or further hearing instructions and check for an email from SFMTA with hearing or decision information.

span.text: If you prefer, you can also call SFMTA Parking Violations at 311 (or 415-701-2311 from outside San Francisco) for assistance. If any page or button label differs from the above, use the site search box on sfmta.org to search for "contest a citation" or "pay or contest parking ticket".
